chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who forgot ṭawāf al-nisāʾ until he returned to his family. He said: He should send someone, and ṭawāf should be performed on his behalf. If he dies before ṭawāf is performed on his behalf, then his guardian should perform ṭawāf on his behalf.

The proper way to understand this report is that it is to be applied to one who is unable to return, for it is permissible for him to instruct someone to perform ṭawāf on his behalf. But as for one who is able to do that, returning is obligatory upon him, as indicated by what the first report contained.

key_terms.تُوُفِّيَ: he passed away before completing the obligation
key_terms.طَوَافَ النِّسَاءِ: the ritual circumambulation of women required in hajj rites
key_terms.لَا يَقْدِرُ عَلَى الرُّجُوعِ: is unable to return to perform the rite personally
key_terms.يُطَافُ عَنْهُ: ṭawāf is performed on his behalf by deputation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone forgets ṭawāf al-nisāʾ and returns home?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling of one who forgets ṭawāf al-nisāʾ until after returning to his family. It states that if he cannot return, he may appoint someone to perform it on his behalf, and if he dies before that, his guardian performs it for him. The compiler clarifies that this deputation applies to inability, while one able to return must do so himself.
